Let me start by evaluating the default configuration (all 'none') as a baseline, then explore promising combinations. Common high-performing NAS architectures often include convolutions and skip connections. Let me start with a baseline.

I need to explore architectures with actual operations. A known good pattern from DARTS/NAS-Bench-201 style search: convolution operations tend to perform well. Let me try an architecture with a mix of convolutions and skip connections, which is typical of high-performing cells.
Let me try a configuration with reasonable operations - a common good pattern includes nor_conv_3x3 and skip_connect.

Thought: Performance jumped to 0.697233 with a mix of convolutions and skip connections. This is much better. Let me explore variations. In NAS-Bench-201, the best architectures often use more convolutions. Let me try an all-convolution architecture to see if it does better.

Thought: All convolutions (nor_conv_3x3) gives 0.709067, slightly better than the mixed version. Let me try variations with nor_conv_1x1 mixed in, and also test skip connections in different positions. In NAS-Bench-201, the optimal architecture often includes a mix. Let me try replacing some 3x3 convs with 1x1 convs, and also try more skip connections.
Let me try a configuration with 1x1 convolutions on some edges.
